questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle in minor segment with center O. C is a point on the minor arc of the circle between the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P. If ∠ACB = 102°, then what is the measure of ∠APB?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ACB = 102°

**Concept Used:**

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de65049b8c3dd4028c6097d211f1fd07850639d986ab92b325f48aa2bd17d051.png] 

Point D is taken on the major arc of the circle. Then, A & D, B & D, C & B, and A & C are joined.

∠ACB = 102°

Now,

∠ADB = (180 – 102)° = 78°

Now,

∠AOB = (78 × 2)° = 156°

Since OA = OB, ΔAOB is an isosceles triangle and ∠OBA = ∠OAB.

Now,

∠AOB + ∠OBA + ∠OAB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OBA = (180 – 156)°

⇒ ∠OBA = 12°

Now,

∠OBA = 12°

∠OAB = 12°

Now,

∠OAP = ∠OAB + ∠BAP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠BAP

⇒ ∠BAP = 78°

Now,

∠OBP = ∠OBA + ∠ABP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠ABP

⇒ ∠ABP = 78°

Now,

∠APB + ∠ABP + ∠BAP = 180°

⇒ ∠APB + 78° + 78° = 180°

⇒ ∠APB = 180° - (2 × 78)°

⇒ ∠APB = 24°

**∴ The required measure of ∠APB is 24°.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked every item 25% above the cost price and allowed 10% discount. Shruti being a regular customer got 5% additional discount on the bill and paid Rs. 2394 for the item purchased. What is the cost price of the item (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Equivalent discount for Shruti = 10 + 5 - (10 × 5)/100 = 14.5%

Let the CP be Rs. 100

MP = 100 + 25 = 125

SP (For shopkeeper) = [125 × (100 - 14.5)]/100 = 106.875% = 2394

⇒ 1% = 22.40

⇒ 100% = Rs. 2240.

**∴ The cost price is Rs. 2240.**

**Traditional method:**

**Given:**

The Shopkeeper marked every item 25% above the cost price and allowed a 10% discount.

Shruti being a regular customer got a 5% additional discount.

She paid a bill of Rs. 2394.

**Concept Used:**

Percentage calculation

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the item purchased by Shruti be P.

Now,

Marked price

⇒ P + P × 25%

⇒ P (1 + 0.25)

⇒ (P × 1.25)

After 10% discount

⇒ (P × 1.25) - (P × 1.25) × 10%

⇒ (P × 1.25) (1 – 0.1)

⇒ (P × 1.25) × 0.9

⇒ (P × 1.125)

After addition 5% discount

⇒ (P × 1.125) - (P × 1.125) × 5%

⇒ (P × 1.125) (1 – 0.05)

⇒ (P × 1.125) × 0.95

⇒ (P × 1.06875)

According to the question,

(P × 1.06875) = 2394

⇒ P = 2394 ÷ 1.06875

⇒ P = 2240

**∴**** The cost price of the item purchased by Shruti is Rs. 2240.**

questions.question: The average of x occurring 5 times and y occurring 7 times is 37. Also, the average of x occurring 7 times and y occurring 5 times is 35. The value of y is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 5x + 7y = 37

Average of 7x + 5y = 35

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/No. of elements

**Calculation:**

5x + 7y = 37 × 12 ----(1)

7x + 5y = 35 × 12 ----(2)

By subtracting eq (2) from eq (1)

2y - 2x = 12 × 2

⇒ y - x = 12

⇒ 5y - 5x = 60 ----(3)

Adding eq (3) with eq (1)

So,

5x + 7y + 5y - 5x = 444 + 60

⇒ 12y = 504

⇒ y = 42

**∴ The value of y is 42**

questions.question: In an examination, 45% of all the students who appeared are boys and the rest are girls. If 60% of the boys and 70% of the girls passed, then what is the percentage of students who failed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total number of students in the examination be 100.

Number of boys = 45, which means number of girls = 55.

Boys who failed = (100 − 60)% of 45 = 40% of 45 = 18.

Girls who failed = (100 − 70)% of 55 = 30% of 55 = 16.5.

Total failed percentage = 18 + 16.5 = 34.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.5%.**

questions.question: If x⁴ + y⁴ + x²y² = 21 and x² + y² - xy = 7, then what is the value of (x)/(y)+(y)/(x)?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

x4 + y4 + x2y2 = (x2 + y2 - xy)(x2 + y2 + xy)

**Calculation:**

Given that, 

x4 + y4 + x2y2 = 21 -----(1)

x2 + y2 - xy = 7 -----(2)

We know that,

x4 + y4 + x2y2 = (x2 + y2 - xy)(x2 + y2 + xy)

Using equation (1) & (2)

⇒ 21 = 7(x2 + y2 + xy)

⇒ (x2 + y2 + xy) = 3 ----(3)

Now.

(x2 + y2 + xy) + (x2 + y2 - xy) = 3 + 7

⇒ **x****2 + y2 = 5**

Put this value in equation (3)

⇒ 5 + xy = 3

⇒ **xy = - 2**

Now, (x)/(y)+(y)/(x) = ( x² + y²)/(xy)

⇒ ​(x)/(y)+(y)/(x)​ = - 5/2

**∴ The required answer is - 5/2**

questions.question: If 3 sin² θ - cos θ - 1 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of cot θ + cosec θ ?

x2 – (sum of roots)x + product of roots = 0

questions.question: if x + y = 3 and (1)/(x)+(1)/(y)=-(3)/(10), then the value of (x² + y²) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x + y = 3

1/x + 1/y = - (3/10)

**Concept Used:**

(A + B)² = A² + 2AB + B²

**Calculation:**

1/x + 1/y = - (3/10)

⇒ (x + y)/xy = - (3/10)

⇒ xy = (-10)

Now,

x + y = 3

⇒ (x + y)² = 9 (Squaring both side)

⇒ x2 + y2 + 2xy = 9

⇒ x2 + y2 = 9 - 2xy

⇒ x2 + y2 = 9 – 2 × (-10)

⇒ x² + y² = 29

**∴ The required value of x² + y² is 29.**

A and B together can complete a certain work in 20 days whereas B and C together can complete it in 24 days. If A is twice as good a workman as C, then in what time will B alone do 40% of the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A = 2C

A + B in 20 days

B + C in 24 days

**Concept used:**

Total work = LCM of time taken by the workers

**Calculation:**

LCM of 20 and 24 is 120

So, efficiency of A and B = 120/20 = 6 and efficiency of B and C = 120/24 = 5

Now 2C + B = 6 and B + C = 5

So, C = 1

B = 4

40% of the work = 120 × 2/5 = 48 units

So, B will take 48/4 = 12 days

**∴ B alone do 40% of the same work in 12 days**

questions.question: Akhil takes 30 minutes extra to cover a distance of 150 km if he drives 10 km/h slower than his usual speed. How much time will be take to drive 90 km if he drives 15 km per hour slower than his usual speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Akhil takes 30 minutes i.e., 1/2 hour extra to cover a distance of 150 km if he drives 10 km/h slower than his usual speed.

**Concept used:**

Time = D/S

D = Distance

T = Time 

**Calculation:**

Let the usual speed of Akhil be S km/h.

After a 10kmph reduction, the speed of Akhil = (S - 10) km/h

According to the question,

150/(S - 10) - 150/S = 1/2

⇒ 150 {1/(S - 10) - 1/S} = 1/2

⇒ 150 {(S - S + 10)/ {S × (S -10)} = 1/2

⇒ 150 {10/ {S × (S - 10)} = 1/2

⇒ S × (S - 10) = 2 × 150 × 10

⇒ S = 60

Now,

Time taken by Akhil to drive 90 km at (60 - 15) km/h i.e. 45km/h

⇒ (90/45) hours

⇒ 2 hours

**∴ Time taken by Akhil to drive 90 km if he drives 15 km per hour slower than his usual speed is 2 hours.**

questions.solution:

Perimeter of a semi circle = πr + 2r

r(π + 2) = 25.7

⇒ r = 5

So, the diameter is 10 cm

**∴ Diameter of the semi circle is 10 cm**
